chunks: And ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, peace be upon them both, the Master of the Worshippers, used to say:
"Al-ʿAfw, Al-ʿAfw (Pardon, pardon)," three hundred times in the Witr at dawn.

key_terms.السَّحَرِ: the pre-dawn time, especially associated with worship and seeking forgiveness
key_terms.الْعَفْوَ: pardon; a plea for divine forgiveness and overlooking of sins
key_terms.الْوَتْرِ: the Witr prayer, the concluding unit of the night prayer
key_terms.ثَلَاثَمِائَةِ مَرَّةٍ: three hundred times; indicating repeated supplication
key_terms.سَيِّدُ الْعَابِدِينَ: Master of the Worshippers; an honorific title of Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام

ai.seo_question: What did Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام recite in the Witr prayer at pre-dawn?
ai.summary: This report describes the practice of Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليهما السلام in the Witr prayer during the pre-dawn hours. It highlights repeated seeking of pardon through the phrase "al-ʿafw," showing the devotional importance of asking Allah for forgiveness in the night prayer.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1408 - It is narrated that Imam Ali ibn al-Hussain (as), the Master of Worshippers (Zain al-Abidin), used to say,
"Al-‘Afw, Al-‘Afw (Pardon, Pardon)" three hundred times during the Witr prayer at the time of Suhoor (the pre-dawn hours).
